s1-guest-layer-lima.deltaSummaryMarkdown: Inspected the delta in src/setup/lima.rs, tests/setup_lima.rs and tests/guest_layer.rs. (1) `doctor_lists_the_ubuntu_pin_with_the_other_pins` renders the real doctor report JSON and asserts `pins.ubuntu` is 24.04/default; the Pins-value claim is dropped and the test renamed `both_guest_names_derive_from_one_pin_value`, consistent with the pin being the constant `DEFAULTS.ubuntu`. (2) `plan_clone` runs in `run_with` right after the macOS, Homebrew and home checks and before `ensure_lima`, any `limactl` call, create/start or guest step; it refuses a missing checkout, one outside the home, and an unsafe target, and the new test uses a Mac without Lima and asserts no change command and no guest script for each case. The exact refusal text is unchanged. (3) `lima::detect_checkout` returns NotMacOs before any command off macOS and runs git only with `--clone`; `lima::run` uses it and exits 1; the test asserts an empty recorded spec list off macOS and without `--clone`. The create/start arguments, `--check` behaviour and clone script are untouched; both sprint groups pass on the new snapshot.
s1-guest-layer-lima.summaryMarkdown: Source review: the pin lives only in `project::pins`; `setup::guest` is a faithful move of the WSL operations (same scripts, `--exec`/`--workdir /` quoting, installer, override, clone, inner setup) and the WSL sequence and clones-file changes are covered; `lima.rs` builds the exact create/start arguments, only touches instance `rayx`, runs no `sudo`, and `--check` runs only reads (also proved end to end with stand-in tools; `limactl shell` without `--start` cannot start a stopped VM in Lima 2.2.1). Failed on one coverage gap (doctor pin listing untested, PIN-1) and two minor ordering defects (late clone validation, git queries on non-macOS). Everything else in GST-1, LIMA-1..4 is met by source and meaningful tests.

s2-sizing-records-doctor.deltaSummaryMarkdown: Inspected the repair delta. f1: lima::record_outcome and wsl::record_outcome return early on --check and are what lima::run/wsl::run call; new tests assert --check writes nothing and reads nothing from the guest, a real run records flags, VM and clone, the WSL record and clone_record, the LimaOutcome for create/edit/unchanged/clone, and the end-to-end `rayx setup --lima --check` asserts no ~/.config/rayx. f2: customize keeps an already-writable home without asking (tested). f3: LimaOutcome.vm is always the VM's actual settings with the home from lima.yaml (tested for unchanged and edited). f4: invalid-UTF-8 guests.json is Unparsable and left byte-identical (tested); record_run keeps the record's previous ubuntu when the version is unreadable (tested). Re-ran setup_lima_sizing, setup_lima_edit, guest_records and setup_lima: all pass. No regressions seen in LIMA-5/6/7 or DOC-1.
s2-sizing-records-doctor.summaryMarkdown: LIMA-5, LIMA-6, LIMA-7 and DOC-1 are implemented as specified and covered by meaningful tests (caps, notes, refusal before any limactl/brew command, free-space and memory warnings, the single Customize question flow, stop/edit/start sequence, shrink refusal, doctor text/JSON for running, stopped, retired, missing, Lima missing, WSL on Windows, read-only). REC-1's file format, merge, atomic write and missing/unparsable handling are correct and tested, and --check is correctly skipped at both call sites in source, but the wiring from a real run into the record (and the --check skip) has no test, so REC-1 is not proven. Minor issues are listed.

s3-update-refresh.deltaSummaryMarkdown: Inspected the repair delta. `HostUpdate.unreadable` is set by `update_host` when `setup.json` cannot be parsed (code 1, recorded false). `RefreshReport.unreadable` is set by `refresh_guests` when `guests.json` cannot be parsed, and `RefreshReport::code()` is 1 then. `setup::update::run` prints the nothing-recorded message only when neither record was unreadable and nothing was refreshed. New tests cover the host case (`an_unparsable_setup_record_is_an_error_not_nothing_recorded`), the real binary exiting 1 without the message, and the refresh case (`an_unparsable_guest_record_fails_the_refresh_instead_of_refreshing_nothing`, which also asserts no commands ran). Earlier-reviewed behaviour (records, per-root update, guest refresh order, self-update refresh) is unchanged in the delta.
s3-update-refresh.summaryMarkdown: Failed on one minor but real defect (open finding); the four criteria are otherwise implemented and meaningfully tested in their own new groups. REC-2: `after_run` records only after a code-0, non-check, non-update `rayx setup` (the `--wsl`/`--lima` outer runs return before it), unions sets and roots, and `record_setup` reads before writing so an unparsable file is untouched. UPD-1: `update_host` runs `run_sets` per existing root with `environment_for(Project::discover(root))` (tests prove two roots' different nightly pins), drops vanished roots (not in `--check`), runs once with no project when none is recorded, host never gets `apt-get upgrade` (only `refresh.rs` does, inside a recorded guest), conflicts are clap-enforced. UPD-2: question text, `--yes`/no-terminal, Lima start/stop around the refresh including after failure, Ubuntu check (older guests reported Outdated, exit 1, until migration lands), Linux rayx, apt update/upgrade (`-y` only with `--yes`, interactive), inner `setup --update [--yes]`, continue after a failing guest, `--check` read-only (a stopped Lima VM or WSL distro is not inspected). SUR-1: executable captured before `install()`, exact question and hint, `--yes`, refresh exit code propagated, no refresh for `--check`/up to date/failed install/no records. fmt and clippy are clean. Non-blocking observations: the open minor finding above; `refresh_one` proceeds without a question when the prompter is `None` (production always passes one); `self update --check --yes` is rejected by clap (deliberate and tested, but not in SUR-1); the outdated rule inside `--update`, a stopped WSL distro under `--check`, and the exclusion of outer `--wsl`/`--lima` from recording have no dedicated test.

s4-migration-removal.deltaSummaryMarkdown: Inspected the delta in src/setup/migrate.rs, records.rs, refresh.rs, lima/mod.rs, wsl.rs and tests/guest_migration.rs, and ran guest_migration (21), guest_remove (11), guest_refresh (14) and setup_lima (22): all pass. s4-f1: `migrate_lima` returns `Planned` with a printed plan on the resume path under `--check` before any create, clone, setup or record; the new test asserts no create/rename, no `now runs` line and an unchanged record. s4-f2: after consent and before stop/rename `update_guests(.., |_| {})` probes that the record is readable and writable (an unparsable file or missing config dir stops with `rayx was not changed`); a failed post-rename record write renames the VM back or names the manual `limactl rename` command; tests cover the unparsable record and the unwritable directory (the latter is weak but the probe is exercised by code inspection). s4-f3: `GuestRecord.migrating` is set by `rename_and_retire` and cleared by `finish_migration`; `pending_lima` resumes only migrating entries so a plain `rayx lima remove rayx` is not a resume; `refresh_guests` reports a migrating retired VM without a current `rayx` as Failed (exit 1). s4-f4: `setup --lima` reads VERSION_ID after the optional `--vm-*` edit and start (older -> migration, newer -> note); `migrate_older_guest` reads the live VERSION_ID, prints the newer-than-pin note for recorded WSL guests, and the question is exactly `Create <new> with Ubuntu <pin> next to <old>?` with a separate always-printed kept line naming the removal command. The trivial enum test was removed. Residual observation, not a defect: WSL outdated detection still starts from a recorded older version, and a record that is stale in the other direction is not discovered. RM-1/RM-2 are unchanged and still pass.
s4-migration-removal.summaryMarkdown: RM-1 and RM-2 are met: `remove_guest` refuses wrong OS and unrecorded names before anything runs, lists dirty clones only when the guest can be inspected without starting it, asks `Remove <name> and everything in it?`, refuses without terminal and without `--yes`, runs `limactl delete --force` / `wsl --unregister`, drops the record entry and prints the current-guest message; `tests/guest_remove.rs` covers each case. MIG-1..3 are largely implemented and well tested (side-by-side Lima rename/create with the old VM's CPUs/memory/disk/yaml-read home mount, record right after the rename, resume after a failed create, WSL install next to the old distribution with first-user stop and rerun, old entry retired only after the new one is set up, no `do-release-upgrade`, no deletion, retired guests skipped by `refresh_guests`, other instances such as `gpux` untouched). The review fails on two defects reproduced against the working tree: `--check` writes the record on the resume path (s4-f1), and a failed record write after the rename leaves a non-resumable, unremovable orphan (s4-f2); two minor findings (s4-f3, s4-f4) cover the uncovered `setup --update` resume and the MIG-1 reading gaps.

s5-docs-mac-proof.deltaSummaryMarkdown: Docs-only delta; snapshot unchanged. Read docs/manual-verification.md and the new logs 17-host-check.log and 18-host-update.log; no source changed (git shows only the AgentX state file modified); limactl list shows only gpux, no ~/.config/rayx remains. f-s5-host-refresh-unproven: 18-host-update.log shows a real `rayx setup` writing setup.json (base + this checkout), then `setup --update --check` and `--update --yes` printing `==> setup --update: /Users/dinko/work-private/projects/RayX/RayX.CLI` with everything installed / Nothing to do, and doctor `no guests recorded` afterwards; the new `MAN-2 refresh, host` row matches it (everything was already installed, so nothing changed, as the row says). f-s5-claims-not-in-logs: the refresh row now separates the failed `--yes` runs (07, 08), the held run (09, `nothing recorded` explained) and the recorded rerun (10); create/edit command lines are attributed to 01-check.log / 05-edit.log; `now runs Ubuntu 26.04` is confirmed at 13-migrate.log:1775 and the VERSION_ID and guests.json-after-migration facts are explicitly labelled as checked interactively and not saved, which is honest. Residual (not a defect): the inner-setup row's guests.json contents are not saved as a log; doctor in 04-checks.log (which reads that record) and the later refresh logs cover it. f-s5-man1-binary-deviation-unrecorded: the new `Deviations from the criteria text` block states the v1.0.0 release installer, why, which MAN-1 checks ran with the released binary, that the branch binary built in the VM ran the refresh and migration through RAYX_LIMA_BINARY, the staging directory under the Mac home (removed) and the uncommitted 26.04 pin build; acceptable and honest. DOCS-1 unchanged and passing.
s5-docs-mac-proof.summaryMarkdown: DOCS-1 holds: README sections match source (caps `max(1,ncpu-2)`/`max(2,RAM/2)`, 30 GiB disk floor, 10 GiB free, three-quarters warning, prompt and question texts, `setup.json`/`guests.json` locations, refresh and removal behaviour, doctor states), every new flag and subcommand has precise help, tests/readme_guests.rs (6 tests) check real README text and `--help` output (not tautologies; minor weakness: `wsl remove` help only checks `<NAME>`/`--yes`). The `limactl rename --tty=false` fix is genuinely covered: without it the recorded command is `rename rayx rayx-22.04`, so `tests/guest_migration.rs` fails its exact change list and the scripted Lima never renames (the rollback rename path is untested, minor). No pin change is left in `src/project/pins.rs` (`24.04`, `git diff` shows only the AgentX state file). The real Mac proof is largely evidenced (customize prompt, read-only home, second run, doctor, stop/edit/start to 3 CPUs, migration to 26.04 with the clone restored, removals with `gpux` running untouched and refused), but MAN-2's host refresh is not shown, several doc claims have no log behind them, and MAN-1's RAYX_LIMA_BINARY deviation is not recorded as one.

s7-integration-repairs.summaryMarkdown: All five findings of the first review are repaired and re-verified: the RAYX_WSL_BINARY report is wired in update::run and tested through the real binary; a running or recorded-older VM is asked for its Ubuntu before any edit and a refused flag is returned before anything starts; doctor shows guests as unknown with `cannot read Lima` on a failing list; REP-4/REP-6 wording matches RecordError::Unreadable. Scoped groups guest_repairs_flow, guest_repairs_safety, doctor, guest_migration, guest_records, setup_lima, setup_lima_edit pass. Residual: a stopped old VM with no record and non-empty --vm-* flags is still edited before its version is known; REP-1 speaks of the running VM, so it is noted, not a defect.

s6-owner-hosts.summaryMarkdown: MAN-3 is met. The section 'Open: Windows and WSL guest layer' records, for 2026-10-14 on Windows 11 (10.0.26300.9457), WSL 2.6.3.0, `rayx 1.0.0` built from `feat/lima-guests` at `12adb9a` and Ubuntu-24.04 (24.04.4), a concrete result for every clause: `setup --wsl --web --clone --yes` passed twice (release installer, then `RAYX_WSL_BINARY`); `guests.json` lists `Ubuntu-24.04` (kind wsl, flags, clone, retired false); the in-guest clones file and `wsl status`; `rayx doctor` reports `wsl Ubuntu-24.04: running ... Ubuntu 24.04, current`; and the removal refusal. The failed refresh row (release rayx 1.0.0 as the guest binary, `unexpected argument '--update'`, exit 1) is recorded honestly, not as a pass. The explanation holds against the code: `guest::ensure_linux_binary` returns early when `rayx --version` equals `rayx <running version>`, and `refresh_inside` orders binary, then apt upgrade, then inner `setup --update`, which matches 52 packages upgraded and then the flag error. The branch version is 1.0.0 (Cargo.toml), so the guest's released 1.0.0 matched; any release containing the epic has a higher version and installs the matching binary first. The `RAYX_WSL_BINARY` pass shows the clause 'refreshes it (apt upgrade, inner update)' end to end, and I accept it. Dispositions: MAN-4 deferral and t14 withdrawal match the recorded owner decision 'Defer to a follow-up' (decidedBy owner); the follow-up is concrete (run the two MAN-4 rows after the first release containing the epic and record date, versions, results), the doc rows say so, and nothing undecided is hidden. Observations for follow-up, not findings: the stray `(B` comes from the cargo-dist installer's output; `rayx` sets no DEBIAN_FRONTEND, so apt prints a harmless debconf Dialog fallback and `--yes` could run apt non-interactively.

final.summaryMarkdown: Integrated review of the current code. All active criteria hold together: one Ubuntu literal (src/project/pins.rs, 24.04) with the WSL name and Lima template derived; the guest layer is shared by --wsl and --lima; records strip --check/--yes from stored flags; --check paths print or query read-only (a stopped distribution or VM is never started or entered); migration, refresh, removal and doctor only touch recorded guests (gpux untouched, proven on the Mac); no host sudo or host apt-get upgrade, no do-release-upgrade, no unversioned template:ubuntu; nothing is deleted without lima/wsl remove and a confirmation or --yes. git diff 0c2ff1f..HEAD shows no unexpected or forbidden files (Cargo.toml only moves serde_yaml_ng to normal dependencies). Reran guest_migration, guest_refresh, guest_repairs_flow and guest_repairs_safety (56 tests, all pass). Manual evidence: MAN-1/MAN-2 recorded with logs for this Mac (2026-10-14; the Linux rayx of the first create came from the release installer, a documented deviation, while RAYX_LIMA_BINARY ran in the refresh and migration rows), MAN-3 recorded as owner-run on Windows (2026-10-14). Dispositions acknowledged: MAN-4 deferred and t14-release-proof withdrawn match the owner's recorded choice, and the follow-up (the two deferred rows in docs/manual-verification.md) is concrete and needs a release that does not exist. Non-blocking observations for the coordinator: (1) doctor labels a guest NEWER than the pin as `outdated` (src/doctor/guests.rs state()), while the struct comment says older-than-pin; only reachable after a CLI downgrade; (2) a Lima migration that fails after creating the new VM leaves it unrecorded until the rerun finishes (the refresh reports the interrupted migration honestly, doctor shows only the retired VM); (3) a STOPPED unrecorded older `rayx` VM given --vm-* flags is edited before its Ubuntu is read; (4) at epic completion record the MAN-4 follow-up in .agentx/memory/knowledge/setup/state.md and promote d-guest-layer (it supersedes the 2026-10-14 WSL release-installer decision).

findings.descriptionMarkdown: **Expected:** PIN-1 requires `rayx doctor` to list the Ubuntu pin with the other pins, and the criterion's automated verification is the new group `tests/guest_layer.rs`. **Observed:** `src/doctor.rs` `pin_list` pushes `("ubuntu", p.ubuntu.clone())` (the built binary's `doctor --json` does print `pins.ubuntu = 24.04/default`), but no test in `tests/guest_layer.rs` or `tests/doctor.rs` asserts it; `tests/doctor.rs` checks only other pin keys, so deleting the line would leave every test green. Also, the `a changed pin` test (`both_guest_names_derive_from_the_pin`) passes `pins.ubuntu.value` into the pure helpers by hand: production `distribution()` and `create_command` read `DEFAULTS.ubuntu` through `pinned_ubuntu()`, never a `Pins` value, so that part of the test does not prove the derivation path. **Repair:** add a test to `tests/guest_layer.rs` that renders doctor's JSON (as `tests/doctor.rs` does, `json["pins"]["ubuntu"]` equals `{value: "24.04", source: "default"}`) and, if the names should follow `Pins`, assert through the real consumers (`distribution()` / `create_command`) or document that the pin is the constant `DEFAULTS.ubuntu` and drop the Pins-value claim.

**Expected:** LIMA-4 / d-lima-vm: a `--clone` with a checkout outside the macOS home (or no checkout) exits 1 with `--clone needs a checkout under <home>, which the VM mounts` and, per the design order, `--lima` should not spend a 100 GiB VM and a release download on a request that cannot succeed. **Observed:** the refusal is made inside `lima::clone_checkout`, after `limactl create`, `limactl start` and `ensure_linux_binary` have already run (`tests/setup_lima.rs::a_checkout_outside_the_home_or_none_at_all_stops_the_clone` only exercises an already running VM, so it cannot see this). **Repair:** in `lima::run_with`, validate the clone request (checkout present, under `home`, `linux_dir` of the requested target) right after the host checks and before the create/start step; extend the test to an absent VM and assert `changes(&runner)` is empty.

**Expected:** LIMA-1: on Windows or Linux `setup --lima` exits 1 with the macOS message and runs nothing. **Observed:** `lima::run` (like `wsl::run`) calls `guest::detect_checkout`, which executes `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and `--abbrev-ref HEAD`, before `run_with` reaches its `host.os != MacOs` check; the test `off_macos_it_exits_before_running_anything` calls `run_with` directly, so the real entry path is unproved. **Repair:** in `lima::run`, return the `LimaError::NotMacOs` message (exit 1) when `host.os != Os::MacOs` before building the runner or detecting the checkout, or detect the checkout lazily only when `--clone` is set; add a check that goes through `run`/the binary on a non-macOS host stand-in, or keep the unit test and assert the ordering in `run`.

Expected: REC-1 ("a successful setup --wsl or --lima (not --check) records the guest ... for Lima the settings it was created with") is verified by tests/guest_records.rs. Observed: the tests call record_guest/GuestsFile::upsert with hand-built GuestUpdate values and record_run once with a hand-built call. Nothing tests (a) that lima::run / wsl::run skip recording under --check (the only guard is the `if !request.check` / `if !args.check` at the call sites; record_guest's dry_run=true parameter is never passed true in production, so the dry-run test does not exercise it), (b) that LimaOutcome.vm carries the created or edited settings (no test in setup_lima_sizing.rs/setup_lima_edit.rs asserts the returned LimaOutcome), or (c) that LimaOutcome.clone / wsl::clone_record produce the CloneRecord (source, branch, target). Removing the --check guard, or dropping `vm` from the outcome, would pass every test. Repair: in tests/guest_records.rs (REC-1's own group) add (1) an end-to-end run of the real `rayx setup --lima --check` binary (the stub-limactl pattern of setup_lima.rs, HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME in a tempdir) asserting no guests.json or config directory is created; (2) assertions on the LimaOutcome returned by run_with for create (settings after caps/customize), edit (changed values merged with the instance's), unchanged VM (None) and --clone (CloneRecord fields); (3) a unit for wsl::clone_record if it can be made pub, or an equivalent assertion. Better still, make the --check decision testable by moving the record call into a function that takes the Runner/dry-run state.

Expected: customizing keeps what the owner already chose. Observed: in sizing::customize the final `Mount the home writable? [y/N]` question always starts from no, so `rayx setup --lima --vm-home-writable`, answering y to Customize and pressing Enter on the home question silently creates a read-only mount, contradicting the flag and the summary line it printed (`home mounted writable`). Repair: when settings.home_writable is already true (flag), either skip that question or treat Enter as keeping writable (e.g. `chosen.home_writable = settings.home_writable || prompter.confirm(...)`, or ask only when it is false); add a case to the customize tests.

Expected: a Lima guest entry carries the VM settings. Observed: when `rayx setup --lima` finds a VM `rayx` that already exists with no explicit --vm-* change (for example the VM created by the already-committed sprint 1 build, which wrote no record), LimaOutcome.vm is None and the new entry is written without `vm`, so the record never gets the settings and later guest work (migration restores flags and clones, and must recreate the VM) has nothing to restore from. Repair: for an existing, unchanged instance return VmRecord built from the instance (cpus, memory_gib, disk_gib, home from lima.yaml) and let upsert set `vm` when the entry has none (keep an existing created-with value otherwise); test it in tests/guest_records.rs.

Expected: an unparsable guests.json is reported and left untouched; only a missing or unreadable file is empty. Observed: read_guests_at uses `std::fs::read_to_string(path).ok()`, so a file with invalid UTF-8 (std error kind InvalidData) is treated as empty and then replaced by write_guests_at. Likewise record_run silently records the pinned Ubuntu when the guest's VERSION_ID cannot be read, which would mislabel an older guest as current. Repair: map only NotFound/PermissionDenied-style errors to an empty record and an InvalidData error to RecordError::Unparsable; when os_version fails keep the entry's previous `ubuntu` (or report it) instead of assuming the pin. Add a test for the invalid-UTF-8 file.
Unreadable setup.json/guests.json was reported as nothing recorded and a broken guests.json exited 0; now an error with exit 1 and no nothing-recorded message.
